data.title: Premium flagship smartphone prices likely to go up by over 30% by year-end: Counterpoint
data.description:
Prices of premium flagship smartphones are expected to go up by 30 per cent to over ₹1 lakh apiece across most of the brands by end of the year due to a sharp rise in memory chip cost, market research firm Counterpoint said on Friday.

Along with the increase in prices of the devices, consumer expectations are also rising, and consumers are looking for meaningful specifications that can match the desired experience across processing speed of the mobile phones, camera, battery, durability, after-sales service, etc.

"A few years ago, a ₹1-lakh smartphone was a rarity in India. Today, as flagship prices keep rising, this price point is becoming increasingly common. Prices of premium flagship devices are expected to rise by more than 30 per cent by the end of 2026 compared with 2025," Counterpoint Research said in a report.

Memory prices are expected to account for 43 per cent of the total phone cost by year-end compared to 13 per cent in the first quarter of 2025, as per the report.

"Rising DRAM (temporary storage) and NAND costs, driven by AI data centre demand, have pushed memory's share of smartphone BOM (bill of materials) from about 13 per cent in early 2025 to over 40 per cent, prompting smartphone manufacturers to reassess specifications, components and product strategies to manage costs," said Tarun Pathak, Research Director, Counterpoint Research.

According to the report, Oppo flagship devices have seen the highest jump in the range of 82-87 per cent on a year-over-year (YoY) basis.

Ultra-premium segment market leader iPhone prices have gone up by 20-22 per cent YoY.

"There is no single best premium flagship, as consumer priorities vary. As Apple and Samsung flagship prices move towards Rs 2 lakh, tech-focused brands like iQOO and Google are attracting consumers with specifications that are at par but at more competitive prices. Beyond hardware, ecosystem flexibility is becoming an important differentiator, especially for working professionals who tend to carry more than one smartphone in addition to a laptop," the report said.

Market leader Samsung recently increased the price of smartphones in the range of ₹2,000-₹4,000 apiece post Diwali.

Before Diwali, the firm had raised the price of its flagship device Galaxy S26 by 17 per cent.

Chinese smartphone company Xiaomi has also increased the price of devices in the same range after Diwali.

data.title: Sanofi Could Digest Potential Insmed Takeover — Market Talk
data.description: A potential acquisition by Sanofi of U.S. drugmaker Insmed looks doable, digestible and consistent with what the French company's new CEO is aiming for, analysts at Jefferies say in a research note. Bloomberg reported Thursday that Sanofi is considering an acquisition of Insmed. Sanofi declined to comment when contacted by Dow Jones Newswires, and Insmed didn't respond to a request for comment. While a potential Insmed acquisition would rank among the largest biopharma deals in recent years, it isn't out of reach for Sanofi, Jefferies says. Sanofi can probably spend more than 25 billion euros on an acquisition, and Insmed would cost it around 31 billion euros with the typical deal premium, the analysts say. A deal would improve Sanofi's trajectory beyond the patent expiration of blockbuster drug Dupixent, they add. Sanofi shares rise 1.7%. (adria.calatayud@wsj.com)

data.title: Turkey Capacity Utilization Rate Falls Slightly; Business Morale Weakens Further
data.description:
ANKARA (dpa-AFX) - Turkey's manufacturing capacity utilization decreased for the first time in three months in November, while factory confidence worsened further to the lowest level in nearly two years, figures from the central bank showed on Friday.

The capacity utilization rate dropped to 74.4 percent in November from 74.5 percent in October.

The decrease in November was mainly due to lower utilization of durable consumer goods, which dropped to 67.7 percent from 68.5 percent. Capacity utilization for investment goods also declined to 72.5 percent from 73.4 percent, while that for intermediate goods rose slightly to 74.5 percent from 74.4 percent.

The confidence indicator for the manufacturing sector weakened to a 23-month low of 99.2 in November from 99.8 in September. Any score below 100 indicates a pessimistic outlook.

Employment expectations over the next three months weakened in November, with the corresponding index falling to 99.6 from 104.5 in October. The index measuring the current situation of the total amount of orders remained almost unchanged at 85.4, compared to 85.3 in October. However, the output expectations index improved to 109.2 from 107.0.

data.title: Japanese Yen a Key Beneficiary of AI-Related Risk Aversion — Market Talk
data.description: The Japanese yen is best positioned to benefit from risk aversion stemming from concerns over the sustainability of lofty valuations in artificial-intelligence stocks, MUFG Bank's Derek Halpenny says in a note. If U.S. yields fall, global yields could also drop, but Japan now offers higher yields than before, he says. The yen is also a safe haven. data.title: Eurozone Wage Growth Accelerates, But Remains Modest — Update
data.description:
By Paul Hannon

Eurozone wage growth accelerated slightly in the three months through September, but remained modest despite the pickup in inflation triggered by the war between the U.S. and Iran.

The European Central Bank on Friday said wages negotiated by labor unions and similar groups were 2.57% higher in the third quarter than a year earlier, an increase in the annual rate of growth from 2.45% in the three months through June.

Since the start of the war, officials at the ECB have highlighted the outcome of wage negotiations as a key indicator as to whether the jump in energy prices triggered by the conflict is set to keep inflation above their 2% target.

But there are few signs as yet that workers are securing larger pay rises to cover increased energy bills.

"What we don't see at the moment is second-round effects, not yet," Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin said in an interview with CNBC on Thursday. "We need to be vigilant about what will happen and that's the reason we've increased rates in the past."

The ECB raised its key rate in September and June.

The eurozone's annual rate of inflation rose to 4% in October from 1.9% in February, the month in which the war began.

That pickup in the pace of price rises has weakened the spending power of eurozone households, and for the year as a whole the European Commission now estimates that wages adjusted for inflation will increase by just 0.4%, a sharp slowdown from 1.8% in 2025.

It expects real wages to rise at a similarly slow pace next year, with the commission forecasting that compensation per worker will rise at an unchanged pace of 3.5%.

data.title: Wall St futures slip as Anthropic debut fails to reassure AI investors
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures down: Dow 0.2%, S&P 500 0.76%, Nasdaq 1.63%
  • Anthropic down 6.5% a day after its debut
  • Gap gains on Old Navy recovery

US stock futures fell on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes that the high-profile listing could steady an AI trade rattled by growth and valuation concerns, while hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment.

Anthropic shares slid 6.8% in premarket trading after surging more than 17% on Thursday in their highly anticipated market debut. The stock began trading more than 34% above its offer price of $83.

The Claude chatbot creator's IPO was seen as a key test of investor confidence in the AI theme after a bruising few weeks for the sector. Concerns over potentially slower data center expansion, higher borrowing costs and the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have intensified fears about returns on massive spending.

The Nasdaq was 13.6% below its record closing high of October 6.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon , Meta , and Microsoft declined more than 1.8% each, while Alphabet was muted. Amazon and Alphabet are among Anthropic's biggest investors.

Chipmakers were lower, with Nvidia down 2.6%, while Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom , Marvell , and Micron lost between 3.5% and 5.5%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius also dropped more than 5% each.

Data center stocks IREN , Applied Digital and Core Scientific fell between 2.8% and 4%.

At 4:57 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were down 99 points, or 0.2%, and S&P 500 E-minis were down 54.5 points, or 0.76%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 434 points, or 1.63%.

Wall Street's main indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

The selloff in AI-linked stocks has largely overshadowed a strong earnings season.

Of the 462 companies in the S&P 500 to have reported results through Wednesday, 83.5% reported earnings above analyst expectations, according to an analysis from Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

Markets are pricing in a 98.4% chance of an interest rate hike from the central bank at its next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Brent crude prices fell 1.6% and were heading for a third straight weekly loss on expectations of a supply surplus, with crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returning to roughly prewar levels.

Markets were also assessing the outcome of the meeting between Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, after the leaders issued a joint peace declaration that made no mention of the conflict between the US and Iran.

Among other movers, apparel retailer Gap rose 2.5% after its Old Navy brand posted better-than-expected quarterly sales.
